pages.text: Life wireless is the Life system's mirror of the akaishi wireless grid: it $(reset)beams pipe-fed Life Energy straight to distant Input/Output Ports$(reset) — removing the need for long runs of Life Energy pipes.$(br2)$(bold)Structure:$(reset) a $(reset)sealed hollow box$(reset), edge length 5:$(li)Walls: Life Wireless Shell as the base, swappable for the Life Wireless Terminal / Controller$(li)Cavity: exactly 1 Life Wireless Core, plus air or modules of your choice$(li)Once formed, the Life Wireless Terminal acts as the network's energy hub.

$(bold)Bound storage:$(reset) the terminal auto-binds Life Energy Cells within $(reset)1 block outside the structure$(reset) as the network's battery pool; capacity grows by placing more Life Energy Cells beside the structure.$(br2)$(bold)Send & receive:$(reset) pipe Life Energy into an Input Port, then place an Output Port far away and pipe out of it — with both structures formed, energy sent at the input shows up in the pipes at the output, equivalent to a direct pipe.

$(bold)Cavity modules:$(reset) the Dimension Bridge enables cross-dimensional links. The Chunk Loading Frame keeps the terminal and authenticated Input/Output Port chunks loaded; adding the Range Module expands each loaded area to $(reset)3×3 chunks$(reset).$(br2)The Input Loss Suppressor affects only input loss, while the Output Loss Suppressor affects only terminal-to-output loss. Both stack linearly from configuration, capped at $(reset)90%$(reset) reduction per direction.

$(bold)Relation to akaishi wireless:$(reset) gameplay is identical to the Wireless Akaishi Energy grid — only the energy type differs. Life wireless accepts Life Energy only; akaishi wireless accepts akaishi energy only.$(br2)Modules must stay in the cavity: placing them in a wall breaks the sealed structure and grants no function. Prepare Life Energy pipes, cells and crafting parts, then follow this entry's recipes.
